transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve ruined everything in my life and I don’t deserve to be doing art or working with anyone anymore. I just feel like a complete failure who has let everyone down, and I don't know how to fix it.
Have you ever had periods lasting at least a few days where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, highly active, or like you were on top of the world?
No, I've never really felt super energetic or on top of the world like that. Even during the brief times when the heavy sadness lifted a little bit, I still felt pretty drained and slow.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has this sadness been a constant presence for several years, or does it come and go in distinct waves?

It’s been building for close to two years overall, but this deep sadness really settled in heavily a little over a year ago. It has been mostly constant and has taken up the vast majority of my time, with only very brief, blurry periods where I didn't feel completely weighed down by it.
Before these past two years, have you ever had other distinct periods in your life where you felt deeply depressed for weeks or months, which then completely went away?

No, I haven't ever experienced periods of deep depression like this before the divorce. Prior to these last two years, my life felt pretty stable and I didn't have these kinds of overwhelming feelings.
During this past year while feeling so weighed down, have you also experienced significant changes in your sleep, appetite, or concentration?

Yes, my sleep is terrible—I lie awake for hours with my mind spinning and then wake up at four in the morning with a jolt of dread. My appetite is also a mess; I mostly forget to eat and just pick at toast, which has caused me to lose a lot of weight.
During that first year when these feelings were starting to build, did you still feel down or sad on most days? Or did you have stretches of time where you felt completely like your normal self?

The deep, heavy depression really settled in around the middle of that first year and has mostly stayed with me ever since. I felt down on almost every single day, with only very brief, blurry stretches where I wasn't completely weighed down. I rarely, if ever, felt like my normal self during that time.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of two months or longer where your mood returned completely to normal and you felt entirely free of this sadness?

No, definitely not. The sadness has been mostly constant over the last two years, with only very brief, blurry periods of a few weeks where I wasn't completely weighed down. I haven't had anything close to two months of feeling back to normal.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your art, or do you still find some moments of joy in them?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like gallery openings, pickup soccer, and my art workshops. Now I just spend my time lying on the couch scrolling or staring at the ceiling. Even when I force myself to go to something, I don't get any joy out of it anymore.
To help me understand the timeline better, has this low or down mood been present on most days for a full two years, or has it been less than two years?

No, it hasn't been a full two years of this deep, down mood. It really settled in midway through the first year after my divorce, so it's been going on for well over a year now, probably about a year and a half.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, continuous depressive episode that has lasted for approximately 1.5 years, initiated after a divorce. The presentation is characterized by depressed mood, marked anhedonia, significant weight loss with decreased appetite, severe insomnia, psychomotor slowing/fatigue, and pervasive feelings of worthlessness and guilt. The duration is less than the 2 years required for dysthymia, and there is no history of prior depressive, manic, or hypomanic episodes, making a single depressive episode (F32) the most accurate diagnosis.
